title: Baked Cod
subtitle: Simple herb-crusted cod baked in the oven
excerpt: Thick cod fillets baked with a parsley and lemon crumb topping until the fish is flaking and the crust is golden. Simple, quick, and adaptable.

recipe.sourceNotes: Baked white fish with a breadcrumb crust is a mainstay of British home cooking and appears in most cookbooks since at least the 1960s. The crumb topping does two things: it protects the delicate flesh from drying out and it adds texture and flavour to what is otherwise a mild fish. Cod works best in thick fillets; thin fillets cook before the crumb has time to colour. Haddock is an equally good substitute.

content.text: Pat the cod dry before adding the topping. Any moisture on the surface will prevent the crumb from adhering and will steam the topping rather than crisping it. The cod is done when it flakes cleanly into large white flakes when pressed with a fork. It should feel firm throughout with no translucent area remaining.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Mix the breadcrumbs, parsley, lemon zest, garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl until the crumbs are evenly coated in oil.
Pat the cod fillets dry with kitchen paper. Place on a lined baking tray. Press the crumb mixture firmly onto the top of each fillet in an even layer.

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes depending on thickness, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes when pressed. Squeeze the lemon juice over the top. Serve with green vegetables and new potatoes or chips.
